How Bra Sizes Are Determined: The Complete Sizing Formula

Understand the mathematical relationship between ribcage underbust circumference, breast projection, and international cup progression systems.

The Modern Bra Sizing Formula

A bra size consists of two distinct components: the Band Size (the foundation that anchors the bra around your torso) and the Cup Size (the volume needed to enclose each breast comfortably).

Band Formula

Measure your snug ribcage underbust in inches.

  • If the measurement is an even number (e.g. 32.0"), your band size is 32.
  • If the measurement is an odd number (e.g. 33.0"), check your tight underbust. If you have soft tissue or prefer firm support, round down to 32. If you have a bony, muscular ribcage with little compression, round up to 34.

Cup Differential Formula

Calculate: Difference = Bust Measurement - Underbust Measurement

Difference (Inches) Difference (cm) US Cup UK Cup EU Cup
0 in0 cmAAAAAA
1 in2.5 cmAAA
2 in5.0 cmBBB
3 in7.5 cmCCC
4 in10.0 cmDDD
5 in12.5 cmDDDDE
6 in15.0 cmDDD/FEF
7 in17.5 cmGFG
8 in20.0 cmHFFH
9 in22.5 cmIGI
10 in25.0 cmJGGJ

Frequently Asked Questions

Clear, anatomically sound answers vetted by professional bra fitters.

What does the number in a bra size represent? ▾

The number (e.g. 32, 34, 36) represents your ribcage underbust circumference. In true modern sizing, it matches your snug underbust measurement rounded to the nearest even number.

What does the cup letter represent? ▾

The letter (A, B, C, D...) represents the mathematical difference between your full bust measurement and your underbust measurement. Every 1 inch (2.54 cm) of difference corresponds to one cup letter increase.
